stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key technologies like transformers and safetensors, central to modern AI.

stories.title: Apple sues OpenAI for allegedly stealing hardware secrets
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Apple has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging the theft of proprietary hardware secrets.
The complaint specifically claims a pattern of trade secret theft by OpenAI employees who previously worked at Apple.
The lawsuit also includes IO Products, Jony Ive's hardware venture, as a named defendant.

stories.title: Nvidia’s biggest RAM supplier just had a trillion-dollar debut on Wall Street
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: SK Hynix, a major RAM supplier to the AI boom, successfully debuted on Wall Street.
The company raised $26.5 billion in its IPO, setting a new record for a foreign company debut.
The market performance highlights the massive capital influx and growing importance of memory chip suppliers in the AI ecosystem.

stories.title: Disable autoplay and infinite scroll or risk massive fines, EU tells Meta
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: The EU's Digital Services Act (DSA) is compelling Meta to implement significant platform changes.
Key requirements include disabling autoplay and infinite scroll features.
Failure to comply with these regulations risks substantial financial penalties for Meta.

stories.title: Apple sues OpenAI, accuses ex-employees of stealing trade secrets
stories.author: stock_toaster
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly suing OpenAI.
The lawsuit accuses former employees of stealing trade secrets.
This signals increasing legal tension and intellectual property disputes between major tech players.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI, indicating its primary function.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, suggesting a focus on model deployment and performance benchmarking.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in generative AI tasks.
The associated tags (transformers, llama, safetensors) confirm its relevance within the modern LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a large language model (LLM).
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round involved major investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly growing, currently serving 8.9 million developers in the open models space.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when run through Ollama 0.31.
The speed improvement is achieved via Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging the MLX framework.
Coding agent performance shows up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher quality outputs, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is its local-first architecture, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing AI workloads for Apple devices.
The feature is currently available in preview, signaling a push toward native, high-speed local AI inference on macOS.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The tool leverages Ollama, positioning itself within the growing trend of local, self-hosted AI solutions.

stories.title: Meta turns off the Instagram feature that let users make AI deepfakes of public accounts
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta is disabling an Instagram feature that allowed users to create AI deepfakes from public accounts.
The feature caused significant backlash because it used public account content without explicit owner permission.
This action highlights growing industry concerns regarding AI usage rights and unauthorized content generation.

stories.title: The FCC is cracking down on DJI tech that dodged the foreign drone ban
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: The FCC is actively enforcing regulations against entities suspected of circumventing the US foreign drone ban.
The crackdown targets companies like Xtra and Skyrover, which allegedly help DJI bypass restrictions.
This indicates increased regulatory scrutiny over the importation and distribution of DJI technology in the US.

stories.title: Quantum error correction can constantly recalibrate a processor
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Quantum error correction is being enhanced by continuous recalibration.
Reinforcement learning is employed to utilize error information for algorithm adjustment.
This represents a significant step toward stabilizing and improving quantum processors.

stories.title: Ransomware negotiator hired to represent victims was working for the attackers
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A ransomware negotiator was found to be working for the attackers, betraying his clients.
The individual was sentenced to six years in prison for his actions.
The case highlights severe ethical breaches within the cybersecurity incident response industry.

stories.title: AUTOPILOT VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Incident-Centric Dashcam Understanding
stories.author: Jugal Kalita
bullet_points: Introduces AUTOPILOT-VQA, a new benchmark specifically designed for incident-centric visual question answering in dashcam video.
Addresses a critical gap in current Vision-Language Model (VLM) evaluation: reliably assessing reasoning capabilities for safety-critical driving incidents.
Leverages recent advancements in VLMs and LLMs to push the boundaries of autonomous driving understanding.

stories.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Statistical Characterization of Quantization Effects in LLMs
stories.author: Carson K. Leung
bullet_points: Current LLM evaluation for quantized models is insufficient, relying too heavily on accuracy and perplexity.
The paper introduces 'correctness agreement,' a novel, decision-level metric to assess behavioral changes post-quantization.
This new metric provides a more robust evaluation method for deploying LLMs in resource-constrained environments.

stories.title: Super Weights in LLMs and the Failure of Selective Training
stories.author: Akarsha Sehwag
bullet_points: Identifies 'Super Weights' in LLMs—parameters whose removal drastically degrades model performance.
Challenges the assumption that Super Weight-aware training is effective, showing isolation training causes severe accuracy drops.
Demonstrates that the concept of Super Weights and their importance is not universally applicable across all LLMs.

stories.title: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
stories.author: Xihui Liu
bullet_points: Introduces UniClawBench, a new universal benchmark designed to evaluate proactive agents.
Addresses limitations of current benchmarks, which often use sandboxed environments and single-turn evaluations.
Aims to provide a more rigorous evaluation framework for real-world, complex agent capabilities.

stories.title: WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: WebSwarm introduces a recursive multi-agent orchestration framework to overcome limitations in LLM-based web search.
The research addresses the constraint of single ReAct agents being limited by trajectory length and context window for deep/wide searches.
It aims to improve upon existing multi-agent systems by enhancing recursive depth and search coverage capabilities.

stories.title: UltraX: Refining Pre-Training Data at Scale with Adaptive Programmatic Editing
stories.author: Zhiyuan Liu
bullet_points: Addresses the diminishing returns of scaling laws as training data approaches physical limits for LLMs.
Proposes 'UltraX,' a method for refining pre-training data at scale using adaptive programmatic editing.
Aims to overcome limitations in existing data refinement techniques (rule-based, etc.) regarding quality and efficiency.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically boosting capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The new feature set includes the capability for web search integration in Claude Code.
This enhancement expands the functional scope of Claude Code through advanced agentic capabilities.

stories.title: Disney Plus is reportedly looking into a free streaming tier
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Disney Plus is reportedly exploring the introduction of a free streaming tier.
The idea was mentioned by Adam Smith, Disney's chief product and technology officer.
The specific content that would be available on a free tier remains unclear.

stories.title: China recovered its first reusable rocket and showed a new way to do it
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: China has successfully recovered its first reusable rocket.
The recovery method demonstrates a new approach to reusable rocketry.
The effort is noted as an attempt to replicate technologies pioneered by SpaceX.

stories.title: Firmware update bricks Hue Bridge Pro devices; Philips gives free replacements
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: A firmware update has rendered Hue Bridge Pro devices unusable (bricked).
Philips is providing free replacement units to affected customers.
Users will face the inconvenience of reconfiguring all their smart lighting setups.

stories.title: An orbiting disco ball gave Einstein’s theory its most precise test yet
stories.author: Jacek Krywko
bullet_points: The article discusses a highly precise test of Einstein's theory of General Relativity.
The experiment utilized an orbiting disco ball to measure spacetime distortions caused by Earth's mass.
The findings provide new, precise data regarding how mass warps spacetime, even for planetary bodies.

stories.title: OpenCoF: Learning to Reason Through Video Generation
stories.author: Hongsheng Li
bullet_points: Introduces OpenCoF, a method designed to enable reasoning within video generation models.
Proposes Chain-of-Frame (CoF) reasoning as a temporal alternative to traditional Chain-of-Thought (CoT) methods.
Addresses the limitation of current video generators, which lack specific supervision for complex CoF reasoning.

stories.title: Ideas Have Genomes: Benchmarking Scientific Lineage Reasoning and Lineage-Grounded Idea Generation
stories.author: Xue Yang
bullet_points: Introduces IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a new benchmark for evaluating AI's ability to understand scientific idea lineage.
Addresses the gap in current AI evaluation by modeling scientific ideas as having an 'inheritance structure,' similar to biological genomes.
Focuses on benchmarking scientific lineage reasoning and generating novel ideas grounded in prior work.

stories.title: Using AI-based Learning Assistants in Higher Education: A Large-Scale Descriptive Analysis
stories.author: Valerie Heckel
bullet_points: The study provides a large-scale, objective analysis of AI learning assistant usage (Syntea) in higher education.
It analyzes usage patterns across diverse student demographics, including gender, age, and degree.
The research addresses a gap in current literature by moving beyond small samples and self-reported data to examine actual usage behavior.

stories.title: Workflow as Knowledge: Semantic Persistence for LLM-Mediated Workflows
stories.author: Francesco Zanitti
bullet_points: Proposes a language-independent, conceptual model for managing LLM-mediated workflows.
Focuses on 'Semantic Persistence' to handle complex workflow aspects like tool use, branching, and checkpointing.
Utilizes Lisp-inspired concepts (symbolic forms, object identity) as explanatory frameworks rather than strict implementation rules.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: A new, publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM named AMALIA is introduced for European Portuguese.
AMALIA shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like measuring the moral foundation of authority.
The paper cautions that high agreement only indicates reliability, not necessarily validity, for complex theoretical constructs.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D human pose estimation focuses on geometry, but real-world applications need biomechanical data.
A new lightweight temporal transformer, 'BioModule,' is proposed to bridge the gap between pose estimation and biomechanical attribute prediction.
The technology has significant relevance for fields like rehabilitation, sports science, ergonomics, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Score Accuracy Along the Forward Diffusion Does Not Certify Numerical Stability in Diffusion Sampling
stories.author: Yiwei Zhou
bullet_points: The paper investigates the relationship between forward diffusion marginal error and the numerical stability of the learned reverse-time sampling process.
It demonstrates that achieving small $L^2$ error in the forward marginals does not guarantee the numerical stability of the discrete reverse-time sampler.
The research constructs a smooth score field that is arbitrarily close to the exact reverse process in path-space total variation while maintaining small forward error.

stories.title: SLORR: Simple and Efficient In-Training Low-Rank Regularization
stories.author: Shiwei Liu
bullet_points: SLORR introduces a new, simple, and stateless method for in-training low-rank regularization.
It aims to improve the compressibility of modern neural networks without significant accuracy loss.
SLORR overcomes limitations of existing methods, such as requiring SVDs or modifying model architecture.

stories.title: Dimensionality Reduction Meets Network Science: Sensemaking on UMAP's kNN Graph
stories.author: Dominik Moritz
bullet_points: The research focuses on leveraging the internal k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) graph constructed by UMAP, rather than just its final low-dimensional embedding.
This internal graph preserves the data manifold structure in the original high-dimensional space, avoiding projection distortion.
Applying standard graph algorithms to this hidden graph can enhance data sensemaking capabilities.

stories.title: ARDY: Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation for Interactive Human Motion Generation
stories.author: Davis Rempe
bullet_points: The paper introduces ARDY, a new model for generating realistic 3D human motions.
ARDY aims to bridge the gap between offline methods (high control, slow inference) and online methods (fast inference, low control).
The technology is highly relevant for interactive applications like animation, simulation, and humanoid robotics.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D pose estimation focuses on geometry, but real-world applications need biomechanical data.
A new lightweight temporal transformer, 'BioModule,' is proposed to bridge 3D pose estimation with biomechanical attribute prediction.
The technology has significant relevance for fields like rehabilitation, sports science, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
stories.author: Abhishek Gupta
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of transferring flexible, language-based reasoning capabilities from LLMs to continuous control policies.
Proposes a novel framework, 'Latent Memory Palace,' utilizing Autoregressive Variational Inference to structure information for control.
Aims to bridge the gap between high-level linguistic reasoning and the fine-grained spatial understanding required for precise robotic/control actions.

stories.title: LTM: Large-scale Terrain Model for Wildfire-prone Landscapes
stories.author: Barath Raghavan
bullet_points: Addresses the critical need for accurate 3D terrain mapping in wildfire hazard assessment.
Proposes a multi-modal reconstruction framework to overcome limitations of expensive LiDAR and sparse image-based methods.
Focuses on improving terrain modeling for large-scale, wildfire-prone landscapes.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: Introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM specifically for European Portuguese.
AMALIA shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like defining the moral foundation of authority.
The research highlights the critical distinction between agreement (reliability) and validity when using LLMs for complex theoretical annotation.

stories.title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
stories.author: Zhuokai Zhao
bullet_points: Addresses 'behavioral state decay' in long-horizon AI tasks where crucial information gets lost in expanding trajectories.
Proposes treating memory not as passive retrieval, but as an active intervention mechanism for decision-making.
Focuses on surfacing scattered, decision-relevant state information (facts, goals, prior attempts) to influence agent actions.

stories.title: Do You Need a Frontier Model as a Citation Verifier? Benchmarking Rubric LLMs for Deep-Research Source Attribution
stories.author: Kevin Paul
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of trusting LLM judges (reward models) used in training advanced AI systems.
It specifically benchmarks LLMs on citation quality verification for deep-research systems, ensuring claims are properly sourced.
The research focuses on calibrating the required capability and potential bias of LLMs acting as source attribution verifiers.

stories.title: DominoTree: Conditional Tree-Structured Drafting with Domino for Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Jyh-Shing Roger Jang
bullet_points: Introduces 'DominoTree,' a new method for conditional tree-structured drafting to enhance speculative decoding in LLMs.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods (like DDTree) by incorporating a GRU-based causal correction for path-dependent token distributions.
Aims to accelerate LLM inference by improving the accuracy and structure of the draft tokens generated for parallel verification.

stories.title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
stories.author: Jonathan Amar
bullet_points: The study addresses a critical gap in health chatbot development: the reliance on simulated patients for testing.
Analysis of 2,053 real patient-chatbot conversations revealed high variability in communication patterns and emotional expression among users.
Researchers developed a sophisticated patient simulator that models clinical content, emotional state, conversational strategy, and communication style.

stories.title: It Takes a MAESTRO To Prune Bad Experts
stories.author: Tanmoy Chakraborty
bullet_points: The paper addresses a major deployment bottleneck in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models: the need to keep large expert banks in memory.
Existing pruning methods are insufficient because they use local heuristics that fail to account for the interdependent nature of MoE routing.
The proposed method, MAESTRO, introduces a new approach (Markov-chain App...) to intelligently prune 'bad' experts for improved inference efficiency.

stories.title: QuadRF can spot drones and see WiFi through my wall
stories.author: speckx
bullet_points: QuadRF demonstrates advanced RF sensing capabilities.
The technology can detect drones remotely.
It possesses the ability to penetrate walls to detect WiFi signals.

stories.title: Postgres rewritten in Rust, now passing 100% of the Postgres regression tests
stories.author: github.com via Vaelatern
bullet_points: PostgreSQL has been successfully rewritten in the Rust programming language.
The Rust implementation has achieved 100% passing rate on the original Postgres regression tests.
This signals a significant step in modernizing and potentially improving the performance/safety of a major database system.

stories.title: Cpp2Rust: Automatic Translation of C++ to Safe Rust
stories.author: github.com via gnyeki
bullet_points: The article discusses 'Cpp2Rust,' a tool designed for automatic translation from C++ to Rust.
This addresses the challenge of migrating large, existing C++ codebases to the memory-safe Rust ecosystem.
The focus is on enabling interoperability and modernization between two major systems programming languages.

stories.title: Return on Attention: Why AI Code Reviews Are Wearing Us Out
stories.author: cseeman
bullet_points: The proliferation of AI in code reviews (bots reviewing and replying) is increasing PR volume without improving ticket quality.
The integration of LLMs is leading to automated, sometimes nonsensical, 'arguments' between bots regarding abstract priorities.
The core issue identified by the CEO is broader than just code review, suggesting a systemic problem with current development workflows.

stories.title: Make AI Agents See Your Website
stories.author: kumakint
bullet_points: AI coding agents are increasingly integrated into the developer workflow.
The article discusses the growing presence and impact of these AI agents.
The core topic is enabling AI agents to interact with and 'see' live websites.

stories.title: An Agent That Hunts Bugs in My App While I Sleep
stories.author: debs_obrien
bullet_points: Describes an automated agent designed for continuous software bug hunting.
Highlights the concept of AI/automation operating 24/7 for quality assurance.
The article is presented on Dev.to, suggesting a developer-focused, practical application.
